drhp.business:
SFC Environmental Technologies Limited (SFCTECH) is an environmental technology company offering integrated engineering solutions in wastewater treatment (WWT), wastewater recycling and reuse (WRR) and solid waste treatment (SWT). Revenue from operations was ₹1,339.44 million in Q1 FY2027, ₹8,036.29 million in FY2026, ₹6,978.58 million in FY2025 and ₹6,574.95 million in FY2024.

The WWT segment is built on the proprietary C-Tech technology — an advanced, patented variation of the Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR) process. C-Tech is designed and manufactured in-house and claims over 80% market share in SBR-based WWT solutions in India. As of June 30, 2026, SFC had commissioned 724 C-Tech installations with a combined treatment capacity of 17,464.61 million litres per day (MLD), covering municipalities, industrial operators, real estate developers and commercial establishments. C-Tech’s reported technical advantages include 98% BOD removal efficiency, 40% lower power consumption, 50% smaller land footprint and minimal odour compared with conventional activated sludge processes. SFC also holds the exclusive right from DuPont for the supply of Ultrafiltration (UF), Closed Circuit Reverse Osmosis (CCRO) and Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) membranes to the WWT sector in India, enabling the company to offer end-to-end WRR solutions to customers requiring reuse-quality treated water.

The SWT segment uses the proprietary OREX technology to process municipal solid waste (MSW) into biogas (compressed biogas or CBG) and soil-enhancing by-products. SFC operates two integrated SWT facilities in Goa: a 350 TPD plant at Saligao (running for over 10 years, the longest-operating integrated MSW-to-biogas plant in India) and a 75 TPD plant at Sonsoddo, Margao. In FY2026 the company secured two large CBG orders — 125 TPD at Tinsukia and 300 TPD at Bhubaneswar — with a combined value of ₹5,017.00 million. CBG and related orders represent a new, high-value growth vertical.

Revenue is almost entirely from repeat customers: 97.41% in Q1 FY2027, 91.98% in FY2026, 85.18% in FY2025 and 89.96% in FY2024. The company also manufactures C-MEM hollow-fibre membranes and electronic panels, and Solar Sludge Treatment Cells (STTC) to further reduce lifecycle costs at C-Tech plants.

risks: While our Company and the wastewater treatment industry in India has not experienced any sudden instance of technological disruption in the recent past, (Source: F&S Report) there can be no assurance that technological changes in the future shall not displace our current business offerings.
For example, as per the F&S Report, SBR is a key wastewater treatment technology in India, representing about 28% to 30% of installed capacity for municipal and industrial plants.

Malfunctions of these technologies which are mechanical in nature, including disruptions due to wear and tear, natural or man-made disasters (e.g. terrorism or cyber intrusion) or equipment failure, could interrupt operations, create incremental operational and safety risks or negatively impact our service to our customers and our business reputation.
We are significantly dependent on projects, contracts or works awarded or funded by government entities, either directly or through our private customers.
Our primary customers in these segments are a mix of private and governmental entities.
In the WWT segment, our target customers are private EPC companies who bid for STP projects, serving ultimately municipalities and other government entities that award these projects.

We are currently operating two SWT projects in Goa for the Goa Waste Management Corporation, a Government of Goa undertaking under concession agreements issued to VWTPL for the South Goa Plant for a period of 11.5 years from the date when VWTPL took over the project site for the completion of construction work in 1.5 years and an operational period of 10 years, and to HWTPL for the North Goa Plant for a period of 10 years.

While we were able to extend the concession period for a period of one year until August 20, 2027 or until the subsequent operator assumes the operations and maintenance responsibility following completion of the transition process, whichever is earlier, upon expiry of such period for the North Goa Plant, these concession agreements do not provide for automatic renewal upon expiry of the respective concession periods.

overview.business_model:
SFC Environmental Technologies Limited (SFCTECH) is an environmental technology company offering integrated engineering solutions in wastewater treatment (WWT), wastewater recycling and reuse (WRR) and solid waste treatment (SWT). Revenue from operations was ₹1,339.44 million in Q1 FY2027, ₹8,036.29 million in FY2026, ₹6,978.58 million in FY2025 and ₹6,574.95 million in FY2024.

The WWT segment is built on the proprietary C-Tech technology — an advanced, patented variation of the Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR) process. C-Tech is designed and manufactured in-house and claims over 80% market share in SBR-based WWT solutions in India. As of June 30, 2026, SFC had commissioned 724 C-Tech installations with a combined treatment capacity of 17,464.61 million litres per day (MLD), covering municipalities, industrial operators, real estate developers and commercial establishments. C-Tech’s reported technical advantages include 98% BOD removal efficiency, 40% lower power consumption, 50% smaller land footprint and minimal odour compared with conventional activated sludge processes. SFC also holds the exclusive right from DuPont for the supply of Ultrafiltration (UF), Closed Circuit Reverse Osmosis (CCRO) and Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) membranes to the WWT sector in India, enabling the company to offer end-to-end WRR solutions to customers requiring reuse-quality treated water.

The SWT segment uses the proprietary OREX technology to process municipal solid waste (MSW) into biogas (compressed biogas or CBG) and soil-enhancing by-products. SFC operates two integrated SWT facilities in Goa: a 350 TPD plant at Saligao (running for over 10 years, the longest-operating integrated MSW-to-biogas plant in India) and a 75 TPD plant at Sonsoddo, Margao. In FY2026 the company secured two large CBG orders — 125 TPD at Tinsukia and 300 TPD at Bhubaneswar — with a combined value of ₹5,017.00 million. CBG and related orders represent a new, high-value growth vertical.

Revenue is almost entirely from repeat customers: 97.41% in Q1 FY2027, 91.98% in FY2026, 85.18% in FY2025 and 89.96% in FY2024. The company also manufactures C-MEM hollow-fibre membranes and electronic panels, and Solar Sludge Treatment Cells (STTC) to further reduce lifecycle costs at C-Tech plants.
overview.business_overview:
We are an environmental technology company offering efficient technologies and comprehensive engineering solutions in the field of wastewater treatment (“WWT”), wastewater recycling & reuse (“WRR”) and solid waste treatment (“SWT”).

Wastewater Treatment (WWT)

Our SBR technology: C-Tech has been implemented in the large-scale SBR-based STPs in India, including one of the largest STP under development, which has a treatment capacity of 424 MLD wastewater, as of July 31, 2026. (Source: F&S Report) In addition to our C-Tech package, we offer high-efficiency turbo blowers for aeration in wastewater treatment, fibre disc filters for efficient removal of suspended solids from wastewater and solar sludge drying systems to efficiently dry sludge from wastewater and solid waste treatment using solar energy. Additionally, our Company has entered into an exclusive supply agreement with DSP Singapore Holdings Pte Ltd (“DuPont”) in August 2024 along with an amendment agreement in June 2025 for membrane aerated biofilm reactor technology (OXYFAS & OXYFILM), which are used to enhance efficiency and capacity of existing wastewater treatment plant, particularly for overloaded or outdated facilities.

Wastewater Recycling and Reuse (WRR)

Building on our secondary wastewater treatment capabilities, we have recently expanded into tertiary treatment solutions. Our wastewater recycling and reuse offerings include design, engineering, manufacturing, procuring, supply, installation and commissioning of projects / plants based on ultrafiltration (UF), closed circuit reverse osmosis (CCRO), and membrane bioreactor technologies (MBR). We have entered into an exclusive supply agreement with DSP Singapore Holdings Pte Ltd (“DuPont”) for the exclusive distribution in India of certain WRR components in the municipal wastewater treatment plants market viz.: (i) membranes for submerged UF (Modules L20N V2 & S10N V2), (ii) CCRO technology, and (iii) B50N MBR modules (MBR).

Leveraging our established leadership and distribution network in WWT and an exclusive supply arrangement with DuPont, we have expanded into the WRR segment as an extension of our core business. The WRR segment is expected to witness significant growth, driven by increasing water scarcity and government initiatives focused on water conservation in India. (Source: F&S Report) Following our expansion into the WRR segment, our order book for the WRR segment stood at ₹5,610.72 million as on August 31, 2026.

Solid Waste Treatment (SWT)

Our Company offers technology solutions for SWT plants comprising of design, engineering, financing, construction, supply and installation, commissioning, performance run, turnkey solutions and operations and maintenance (“O&M”). We are among the market leaders in the municipal solid waste space basis our operational results and comprehensive solutions. (Source: F&S Report) Our principal technology for solid waste treatment is the Organic Extraction (“OREX”) technology. OREX is our proprietary technology, designed to efficiently separate biodegradable organics from inorganic materials and lignocellulosic fibres from mixed municipal waste. (Source: F&S Report) We are among the select few players who have leveraged global technology in the municipal solid waste space and transformed it to be suitable for Indian needs. summary.business:
SFC Environmental Technologies Limited (SFCTECH) is an environmental technology company offering integrated engineering solutions in wastewater treatment (WWT), wastewater recycling and reuse (WRR) and solid waste treatment (SWT). Revenue from operations was ₹1,339.44 million in Q1 FY2027, ₹8,036.29 million in FY2026, ₹6,978.58 million in FY2025 and ₹6,574.95 million in FY2024.

The WWT segment is built on the proprietary C-Tech technology — an advanced, patented variation of the Sequencing Batch Reactor (SBR) process. C-Tech is designed and manufactured in-house and claims over 80% market share in SBR-based WWT solutions in India. As of June 30, 2026, SFC had commissioned 724 C-Tech installations with a combined treatment capacity of 17,464.61 million litres per day (MLD), covering municipalities, industrial operators, real estate developers and commercial establishments. C-Tech’s reported technical advantages include 98% BOD removal efficiency, 40% lower power consumption, 50% smaller land footprint and minimal odour compared with conventional activated sludge processes. SFC also holds the exclusive right from DuPont for the supply of Ultrafiltration (UF), Closed Circuit Reverse Osmosis (CCRO) and Membrane Bioreactor (MBR) membranes to the WWT sector in India, enabling the company to offer end-to-end WRR solutions to customers requiring reuse-quality treated water.

The SWT segment uses the proprietary OREX technology to process municipal solid waste (MSW) into biogas (compressed biogas or CBG) and soil-enhancing by-products. SFC operates two integrated SWT facilities in Goa: a 350 TPD plant at Saligao (running for over 10 years, the longest-operating integrated MSW-to-biogas plant in India) and a 75 TPD plant at Sonsoddo, Margao. In FY2026 the company secured two large CBG orders — 125 TPD at Tinsukia and 300 TPD at Bhubaneswar — with a combined value of ₹5,017.00 million. CBG and related orders represent a new, high-value growth vertical.

Revenue is almost entirely from repeat customers: 97.41% in Q1 FY2027, 91.98% in FY2026, 85.18% in FY2025 and 89.96% in FY2024. The company also manufactures C-MEM hollow-fibre membranes and electronic panels, and Solar Sludge Treatment Cells (STTC) to further reduce lifecycle costs at C-Tech plants.
